comments.author: kixiQu
comments.story: Geniuses of the past were aristocratically tutored
comments.why: Example of autotune as aesthetic choice by capable vocalist
comments.text: Pop performers are optimizing for something outside what hits a recording -- that is to say, in the same way that opera singers have to have some theatrical ability in addition to singing the music, pop performance these days involves a huge amount of choreographed dance. A pop singer I'll not name performed on a late night show and was a target of internet ribbing for having brought only some semi-awkward samba-like side-stepping -- though it's more than I or the karaoke singers could do! Once you start looking at the best singer-dancers rather than the best singers, you'll get closer to the real prerequisites for that genre. (And of course, "the obviously artificial sound" can be an aesthetic choice made by vocalists fully capable of recording impeccable vocals: [VIDEO] )

comments.author: Apocryphon
comments.story: Is old music killing new music?
comments.why: T-Pain's natural singing voice on display
comments.text: Is autotune ubiquitous? Other than the trend of artists like T-Pain who used it for stylistic effect (who actually has a great natural singing voice- [VIDEO] ), I don't think it was ever overwhelmingly used except in certain genres such as EDM. Any ignorance of Kanye West song names may simply be a reflection of his more avant-garde new albums not having the same memorable hooks as old ones, but I can at least think of one recent song by him ("Donda").
